title: Best Kitchen Trash Cans 2026: Ranked by Real Customer Ratings
description: The best-rated kitchen trash cans on Amazon, ranked by real customer ratings on lid design, capacity, and value. Find the right can for a big household, a slim kitchen, or touchless convenience.
quickAnswer: The SONGMICS 13 Gallon Stainless Steel Step-On Pedal can is the most-loved everyday kitchen can in this roundup, holding a 4.5-star Amazon rating with a sturdy stainless build, quiet-close lid, and an under-$70 price. If you want automatic convenience, the Ninestars 13-gallon motion-sensor can is the best value touchless pick, and for a large kitchen or commercial feel, the EKO Urban 24-gallon is the top-rated tall can.

howWeChose.heading: How We Chose These Cans
howWeChose.intro: We rank products the honest way: by digging through real Amazon customer reviews. Here is our process:
steps: Star-rating analysis: We surface the top-rated kitchen trash cans in the category and note their real Amazon ratings.

Review reading: We read through hundreds of verified buyer reviews to find which cans hold up — lids that stay shut, foot pedals that don't snap, sensors that keep working — and which ones buyers warn against.
Lid & use-case matching: We break down the real differences between step-on, automatic, flip-top, and soft-close designs based on how buyers actually use them.
Value matching: We rank the best option for big households, small and slim kitchens, and touchless convenience.
howWeChose.closing: Each product's rating below is its real Amazon rating — a reflection of what real buyers reported, not our own hands-on testing.

whoThisIsFor: This guide is for anyone buying a kitchen trash can who is tired of a flimsy one that tips over, smells, or won't keep the lid shut. Whether you want a simple step-on can or a touchless model, we've ranked options for every kitchen size and budget.
We focused on cans between 12 and 24 gallons that suit typical household kitchens, and we cover slim, dual-compartment, and automatic designs for different needs.

grid.p: Open with a foot pedal so you don't touch the lid. Simple and reliable, and they tend to hold the lid shut well. The classic, no-fail choice for most kitchens.
Open hands-free with a sensor wave. Convenient and hygienic, but they need batteries or power and the sensors are an extra thing that can break over time.
Split trash and recycling into two bins in one footprint. Great if you don't have room for a separate recycling bin.
Lids that close gently on a slow hinge, or a flip-top opening. Quieter and look nicer, but usually cost more and can allow more odor to escape than a sealed step-on.

items: Capacity: Most kitchen cans are 12-13 gallons, emptied a couple times a week for a small household. Big families or food-heavy kitchens may want 20-24 gallons. Slim cans trade capacity for a narrower footprint.
Lid keeps shut: A can whose lid stays closed matters for odor and pets. Step-on and sensor cans generally seal best; flip-tops leak more odor.
Material: Stainless steel is durable and looks premium but shows fingerprints and scratches. Plastic is lighter, cheaper, and quieter but can crack and hold odors.
Odor control: Some cans come with odor filters, deodorizer packs, or treated lids. If smells are a concern, look for a model with a sealed lid and an odor-neutralizing feature.
Rating density: A high star rating across thousands of reviews is a stronger signal than a high rating on a handful of reviews.

care.heading: Care & Maintenance
care.intro: Keep your kitchen trash can clean and odor-free with these tips:
items: Wipe after emptying: Give the inside a quick wipe with soapy water each time you take out the bag to stop residue and smells building up.
Change the bag often: Don't wait for an overstuffed can — frequent bag changes keep both odor and cleaning effort down.
Handle sensors gently: For automatic cans, keep the sensor area clear of grime and replace batteries before they die so the lid keeps working.
Deodorize regularly: If your can has an odor filter or deodorizer pack, replace it per the instructions, or sprinkle baking soda in the bottom of the empty can.
Clean stainless without streaks: Use a soft cloth and a mild stainless cleaner, wiping with the grain, to keep fingerprints and scratches less visible.

faqs.q: What size kitchen trash can do I need?
faqs.a: The most common household kitchen can is 12-13 gallons, which most households empty once or twice a week. Bigger households or kitchens that generate lots of food waste often prefer 20-24 gallons to avoid emptying daily. If counter space is tight, a slim 12-gallon can still fits between cabinets.

faqs.q: Are motion-sensor trash cans worth it?
faqs.a: For hands-free convenience they are worth it for many people, especially while cooking with messy hands. The tradeoffs are battery or power needs and an extra sensor mechanism that can fail over time. A quality automatic can with decent reviews (like the Ninestars) is a solid value; very cheap ones tend to have unreliable sensors.

faqs.q: How do I keep a trash can from smelling?
faqs.a: Empty it regularly, wipe the interior when you change the bag, and choose a can with a lid that actually seals shut. Some models have odor filters, deodorizer packs, or treated lids. A sprinkle of baking soda in the bottom of the empty can also absorbs odors between cleanings.

faqs.q: Stainless steel or plastic trash can?
faqs.a: Stainless steel is more durable, holds a premium look, and resists absorbing odors, but it shows fingerprints and scratches and costs more. Plastic is lighter, quieter, and cheaper but can crack and soak up odors over time. For a long-lived kitchen main, stainless is usually worth the extra cost.

faqs.q: What is a dual-compartment trash can?
faqs.a: A dual-compartment can splits its footprint into two bins — typically a larger trash side and a smaller recycling side — so you can sort waste in one place without dedicating floor space to a separate recycling bin. They are ideal for kitchens where a second bin would be cramped.
